The petitioner/accused is before this Court seeking grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.PC in Crime No.106/2022 of Manchenahalli Police Station, pending in Spl.C.No.79/2002 on the file of the learned Additional District and Sessions Judge, Fast Track Special Court (POCSO),
Chikkaballapura, registered for the offences punishable under Section 376(2)(i), 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act.

Chikkaballapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard Sri Tigadi Veeranna Gadigeppa, learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt. Waheeda M.M., learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
Perused the materials on record.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is the sole accused.
He is innocent and has not committed any offences as alleged.
He has been falsely implicated in the matter without any basis.
He was apprehended on 26.05.2022.

Since then, he is in judicial NC:
2024:KHC:6592 custody.
Petitioner had earlier filed similar petition in Crl.P No.9579/2022.
Same came to be dismissed vide order dated 13.01.2023.
While dismissing the said petition, liberty was reserved with the petitioner to move the trial Court with similar petition after examination of the victim.
Now the victim is examined as PW-1.
She has not supported the case of the prosecution.
On the other hand, she stated that the accused has not committed any offence.
Under such circumstances, there is no reason to detain the petitioner in custody.
He is the permanent resident of the address mentioned in the cause title to the petition and is ready and willing to abide by any of the conditions that would be imposed by this Court.
Hence, he prays to allow the petition.
4. Per contra, learned HCGP opposing the petition submitted that serious allegations are made against the petitioner for having committed the offence.
Victim was aged 14 years at the time of commission of offence.
The medical records support the contention of the prosecution.
The victim has given history of the injury before the Medical Officer.
Her statement under Section 164 of Cr.PC is also recorded.
Under NC: 2024:KHC:6592 such circumstances, the petitioner is not entitled for grant of bail.
Accordingly, she prays for dismissal of the petition.

sentences.text: In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is "Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.PC?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 6.
The mother of the victim lodged first information against the petitioner making specific allegations.
Victim was aged 14 years at the time of commission of offence.
Her statement both under Section 161 and 164 were recorded.
The medical reports support the contention of the prosecution.
Considering all these facts and circumstances, Crl.P.No.9579/2022 filed by the petitioner was dismissed.
However, liberty was reserved with the petitioner to file similar petition before the trial Court after examining the victim.
Learned counsel produced copy of the deposition of the victim who was examined as PW-1 before the trial Court.
It discloses that she has not supported the case of the prosecution even when she was cross-examined by the prosecution.
Under such circumstances, I do not find any reason to detain the petitioner in custody as the same would amount to infringement of his right to life and liberty.

Hence, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled to be enlarged on bail subject to conditions,
which will take care of the interest of the prosecution.
8.

Accordingly, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition is allowed.

Petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.106/2022 of Manchenalli Police Station, Chikkaballapur, on obtaining the bond in a sum of Rs.2,00,000/-
(Rupees Two Lakhs only) with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court, subject to the following conditions:
NC: 2024:KHC:6592 a).
The petitioner shall not commit similar offences.
b). The petitioner shall not threaten or tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
c). The petitioner shall appear before the Court as and when required.
If in case, the petitioner violates any of the conditions as stated above, the prosecution will be at liberty to move the Trial Court seeking cancellation of bail.
